chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad, from some of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the saying of Pharaoh: 'Let me kill Moses.'

He was asked, 'Who prevented him?' He said, 'It was due to his legitimacy, because the prophets and the decisive proofs are only killed by the sons of fornication and the adulteresses.' And my father narrated to me, and the group of my scholars, from Sa'd ibn Abdillah ibn Abi Khalaf, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, with this hadith [with these hadiths].
ai.seo_question: Why was Pharaoh prevented from killing Moses according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) elucidates that Pharaoh’s fear of killing Moses stemmed from his legitimate conception, establishing a theological principle that Prophets and Hujjahs are typically slain by those of illegitimate birth or adulteresses. This specific linkage between the killer of Yahya (a.s.) and the killer of Husayn (a.s.) in Kamil al-Ziyarat underscores the continuity of divine proof being eliminated by illegitimate lineage, a theme central to Shia historiography regarding the Ahl al-Bayt.
